messages:
olivia: getting a bunch of 429s for customer `acme-inc` after yesterday's runtime deploy. they use project-scoped API keys behind a NAT’d NAT gateway. billing shows tokens consumed by project, but responses sometimes show X-RateLimit-Scope: org. anyone seen mixed scoping like this?

sam: can you paste a curl + a raw response header? also which auth method — bearer key only or any extra headers?

olivia: curl sample and response (redacted):

```

curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer pk_project_abc123' -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 34.210.45.22' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

< HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
< X-RateLimit-Limit: 30000
< X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
< X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000000
< X-RateLimit-Scope: org
< x-request-id: req_01HXXXXX

```

olivia: note: customer has a project quota of 30k/min and org quota higher; yet responses say scope=org which caused them to hit org-level bucket and throttle others. billing shows token usage credited to project key though.

annie: tagging SRE. quick Qs: is the proxy doing any header rewriting? do we see project_id in auth claims at the ratelimiter stage? can you paste the x-request-id?

olivia: request id above (req_01HXXXXX). proxy is an internal edge that adds X-Forwarded-For. they are behind a cloud NAT so many projects share same egress IP. i can share a small batch of request ids privately.

mike: quick theory: during recent PR we changed scope precedence to prefer IP-derived affinity when multiple identity signals present. NAT means many project keys collapse to same IP and then get aggregated at org scope. if true, that would explain org-scoped 429s even though keys are project-scoped.

sam: can we repro locally? olivia — can you try same request but remove X-Forwarded-For (or set to client IP) and see header change? also try `-H 'X-Project-Id: proj_abc123'` (if you can) to test explicit header.

olivia: repro steps i ran:

1) baseline (with X-Forwarded-For): 429 + X-RateLimit-Scope: org (see above)
2) with no X-Forwarded-For: 429 + X-RateLimit-Scope: project (interesting, remaining matched project bucket)
3) with X-Project-Id header set: project scope, no 429

so it looks like when the proxy sets X-Forwarded-For we end up preferring ip-derived scope.

annie: thanks — that aligns with mike's theory. digging into ratelimiter rollout notes… yep, PR #4523 introduced a configurable precedence: ip_affinity > api_key_binding > org_fallback. default was switched for a short window during canary. seems the canary reached some edge infra nodes handling this customer's traffic.

support-bot: ticket #SUP-45211 created and auto-escalated to eng-sre. ETA assigned: P1 triage.

annie: mitigation options:
- revert precedence quickly (hotfix) to api_key_binding > ip_affinity > org_fallback (recommended)
- temporary customer workaround: ensure requests include X-Project-Id or use project-specific egress IPs
- long-term: add a safety rule that explicit authenticated project bindings always win unless customer opted into ip_affinity aggregation

mike: note on billing: tokens are billed to the key/project because billing logic uses the API key's claim. rate-limiter aggregation at org only affects availability not billing. so no billing break, but availability degraded. we should check if any throttles caused retries that inflated cost for that customer.

sam: can we confirm which nodes were on the canary? olivia can you DM me two sample request ids and timestamps and i'll correlate to nodes?

olivia: DM'd the ids. also adding link to the customer's support ticket and the timeline: they reported errors 2026-03-16 18:03–18:22 UTC coinciding with the canary window.

annie: patch rolled to revert precedence on the ratelimiter config at 2026-03-17 02:10 UTC on the edge pool that hit the canary. after revert we saw project scope applied and 429s cleared for the customer.

mike: action items:
- [P0] revert config (done)
- [P1] add explicit-unit tests for precedence permutations in ratelimiter PRs
- [P1] telemetry: emit metric `rate_limit.scope_mismatch` when billing key != applied_scope
- [P2] docs: update runbook about NAT customers and recommended workarounds (X-Project-Id, egress IPs)

sam: support followup: i'll email customer explaining root cause (canary config change caused IP-precedence aggregation), the mitigation we applied (reverted precedence), and suggested short-term workarounds. also offering a one-time credits if they had elevated retries.

olivia: thanks all. customer confirmed errors stopped ~10m after revert. please keep the ticket open until telemetry shows no recurrences for 48h.

annie: marking SRE investigation complete and adding an RFC to prevent future accidental precedence flips. will post RFC link in this thread when ready.

olivia: great — closing loop on this side. thanks for quick turnaround :thumbsup:
